title: The player's city
theme: Reactions to what the player builds, plus displacement and closures: homes demolished, workplaces removed, new people moving in.

storylets.title: The first ride on the new line
storylets.note: Reacts to the player opening a metro line. Curious first rides.

A.desc: an adult at the metro entrance

b1: {A} stands at the station entrance and studies the fresh paint on the sign.
{A} lingers at the new line's mouth with hands in pockets.
{A} stops in front of the entrance and reads the route map twice.
b2: {A} points at the line map and traces it with one finger.
{A} gestures toward the stairwell and the lit mouth below.
{A} indicates the new line to a passing friend and shrugs.
b3: {A} boards a car on the new line and the doors hiss shut.
{A} rides down and the train pulls out.
{A} takes the first car on the line and is gone.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Ten minutes to the foundry now. Used to be forty."
Overheard: {A} says: "They did not skimp on the lights, I will say that."

storylets.title: A new club and a new crowd
storylets.note: The Neon Dome opens. Curious faces gather.

A.desc: an adult outside a new club

b1: {A} turns a corner and slows at the glow of a new sign.
{A} walks toward a freshly lit entrance, craning.
{A} drifts toward the club door, drawn by the thump.
b2: {A} points up at the neon letters and says something to nobody.
{A} gestures toward the door and the bouncers.
{A} points at a poster by the door and tilts a head.
b3: {A} joins the rope line, eyes on the door.
{A} takes a place at the end of the rope.
{A} steps into the queue and checks the time.

storylets.title: A queue at the new stall
storylets.note: A new food stall draws a crowd.

A.desc: an adult in a new line

b1: {A} joins a line at the newest stall, craning to read the board.
{A} queues behind six others and sniffs the air.
{A} waits in the stall line and counts the people ahead.
{A} reaches the counter and points at the first picture.
b2: {B.desc} ladles something fragrant and slides it across.
{B.desc} serves {A} a bowl and a spoon and says a price.
{B.desc} hands over the first bowl with a small flourish.
{B.desc} serves up quick and moves on to the next.
b3: {A} takes a first mouthful and goes quiet.
{A} eats standing and nods slowly at the bowl.
{A} blows on the broth and samples the edge.
{A} eats with eyebrows high.

storylets.title: Up the new lift
storylets.note: A new lift gets its first riders.

A.desc: an adult at a lift base

b1: {A} stands at the lift base and watches the cab descend.
{A} waits for the lift with a hand on the rail.
{A} stays at the base, head tilted back to follow the cable.
{A} lingers by the new lift doors.
b2: {A} rides the lift up. The cab shrinks against the towers.
{A} takes the lift and the doors slide shut.
{A} steps in and rides the lift to the terrace.
{A} boards the cab and goes up in a hum.

storylets.title: Green where there was dust
storylets.note: A new lawn attracts the first picnickers.

A.desc: an adult on the new lawn

b1: {A} stands at the lawn edge and prods the grass with a toe.
{A} steps onto the new lawn and looks around.
{A} halts at the grass and crouches to touch it.
b2: {A} points at a young sapling and says something to a stranger.
{A} gestures toward the projector post.
{A} indicates a good patch near the pond.
b3: {A} spreads a blanket on the new grass.
{A} lays a cloth down and settles.
{A} drops onto a blanket and lies back.

storylets.title: First sitter on the new bench
storylets.note: A new bench draws the first rest.

A.desc: an adult on a new bench

b1: {A} walks around a new bench and taps it with a knuckle.
{A} stands over the bench and reads the plaque.
{A} stops at the new bench and wipes the slats.
{A} stays at the bench's end and checks the finish.
b2: {A} sits and leans back with a long exhale.
{A} takes a seat and stretches both legs.
{A} eases onto the bench and watches the square.
{A} perches on the new bench and unwraps a snack.

storylets.title: Down from the sky highway
storylets.note: The new dropoff gets its first arrivals.

b1: {A} steps off the lift at the new dropoff with a bag over a shoulder.
{A} comes down to the pad and glances at the sign.
{A} arrives at the dropoff with a cup in each hand.
b2: {A} stands on the pad and gets bearings by the clock tower.
{A} stays at the base of the lift and scans the street.
{A} halts and looks up, then along the block.
b3: {A} sets off toward the square.
{A} walks away from the pad at a brisk pace.
{A} heads down the street, checking a handset.

storylets.title: Strolling the new plaza
storylets.note: A plaza gets its first walkers.

b1: {A} strolls onto the new plaza with a slow, wide circle.
{A} walks the paving in a loose spiral.
{A} crosses the plaza, boots on fresh stone.
{A} meanders along the plaza rim.
b2: {A} points at the pattern in the paving and traces it with a toe.
{A} gestures toward the fountain.
{A} indicates a light fixture and says a word aloud.
{A} points out a sapling to a passing stranger.
b3: {A} sits on the rim of the fountain and trails a hand in the water.
{A} takes a seat on the plaza steps.
{A} drops onto a ledge and lets out a breath.
{A} sits on a low wall and looks around.

storylets.title: A door that is no longer there
storylets.note: The player demolishes a home. The resident is shown carrying what they can. Hearsay carries the rest. Sets the chain flag A:displaced.

A.desc: an adult with all their things

b1: {A} stands at a stretch of bare ground where a door used to be.
{A} stays on the empty plot, turning slowly in place.
{A} stands before a cleared lot with a crate at {A.his} feet.
b2: {A} gathers belongings into crates on the bare ground.
{A} lashes a mattress to a cart and strains at the handle.
{A} carries a lamp and a bundle of clothes from the rubble.
b3: {A} pulls a cart away down the block, looking back once.
{A} walks off with a bundle on each shoulder.
{A} heads for the metro, dragging a crate.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "They gave us a week's notice. Then the crane."
Overheard: {A} says: "Everything I own is on this cart. That's the whole story."

lines: Overheard: {S} says to {L} that {A.desc} lost the house when the crane came. A week's notice and gone.
Overheard: {S} tells {L}: "{A.desc} was living in that block they tore down. Hasn't been seen since."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} lost the place to the demolition and is staying with someone.
Overheard: {S} mentions to {L} that {A.desc} had to clear out when the building came down.
entry: Lost the home when the building was demolished (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Had to leave after the demolition, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Was displaced by the wrecking crew, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: Back to look at the lot
storylets.note: Someone displaced comes back to see the empty ground. Chain: cty.new-place-found.

A.desc: an adult at a cleared lot

b1: {A} comes along the block and slows at a gap in the row.
{A} turns a corner and stops at a cleared plot.
{A} arrives at the lot with a hand over the mouth.
b2: {A} stands at the edge of the bare ground a long while.
{A} stays where the door used to be, hands at sides.
{A} lingers at the lot's fence with eyes lowered.
b3: {A} bends and picks up a small ceramic shard from the dirt.
{A} retrieves a bent key from the rubble and puts it in a pocket.
{A} scoops up a handful of tiles and turns them over.

log: Overheard: {A} says to a passing stranger: "That was my kitchen window, up there."
Overheard: {A} says: "Third floor, left. I painted that door myself."

storylets.title: Keys to somewhere else
storylets.note: Pays off the displacement chain. A new home found; seen only in passing.

A.desc: an adult with a new key

b1: {A} arrives at an unfamiliar door, reading a number on a slip.
{A} comes up to a door with a key held in a fist.
{A} approaches a new home and checks the slip once more.
b2: {A} lugs a crate up the step, then a second.
{A} hauls the last of a cart's load to the door.
{A} carries a lamp and a rolled mat to the threshold.
b3: {A} goes in. The door slides shut behind a crate.
{A} enters and the light inside flicks on.
{A} steps inside with the crate and shoulders the door shut.

lines: Overheard: {S} says to {L} that {A.desc} found a new place over by the lift. Smaller, but dry.
Overheard: {S} tells {L}: "{A.desc} has a new address. Moved last week."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} is settled in somewhere else after the demolition.
Overheard: {S} mentions that {A.desc} took a room across the district.
entry: Found a new home after losing the old one (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Moved into a new place across the district, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Moved into a new place, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: The sign comes down
storylets.note: The player removes a workplace. A worker finds the door gone. Sets A:jobless so the job-hunt chain can start.

A.desc: an adult at a cleared workplace

b1: {A} comes along the block toward the work door with a lunch tin.
{A} walks to the workplace at the usual hour.
{A} turns the corner with a bag and stops short.
b2: {A} stands at bare ground where the workplace used to be.
{A} stays at a cleared lot, tin hanging from one hand.
{A} stands before a stretch of fence and looks up.
b3: {A} reads a printed sheet stuck to the fence, twice.
{A} reads the notice and rubs the back of the neck.
{A} studies a stamped notice taped to the barrier.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "It says closed as of Monday. Monday! It's Tuesday."
Overheard: {A} says: "Eight years. And there's a sheet of paper."

lines: Overheard: {S} says to {L} that {A.desc} lost the job when the whole place was torn down.
Overheard: {S} tells {L}: "{A.desc}'s workplace is gone. Cleared. Nothing but a fence."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} is out of work since the closure.
Overheard: {S} mentions that {A.desc} lost the job when the place shut for good.
entry: Lost the job when the workplace closed (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Found the workplace cleared away, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Lost work in the closure, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: A stranger with a map
storylets.note: Someone has just arrived and walks the block with a paper map.

b1: {A} walks slowly down the block with a duffel on one shoulder.
{A} wanders into the square and turns a full circle.
{A} comes along the sidewalk reading house numbers.
b2: {A} reads a notice board, then a map, then the board again.
{A} stops at a printed sheet and scans it.
{A} checks a folded map against the street signs.
b3: {A} points down a side street and then changes {A.his} mind.
{A} gestures toward the clock tower and asks a stranger the way.
{A} points at the tower and walks toward it.

log: Overheard: {A} asks: "Is this the way to the square? I came in this morning."
Overheard: {A} says: "First day in the city. Is it always this loud?"

lines: Overheard: {S} says to {L} that {A.desc} just got to the city and is still finding the way around.
Overheard: {S} tells {L}: "New in town. {A.desc}. Walks around with a map."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} moved here from elsewhere only last week.
Overheard: {S} mentions that {A.desc} is brand new to the district.
entry: Arrived in the district only days ago (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Came to the district last week, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).

storylets.title: New boxes at the end of the row
storylets.note: A new neighbor moves in; an existing resident watches. Uses the game's own flag.

b1: {A} sits on the stoop with a cup and watches the row.
{A} takes a seat on the step and stretches out.
{A} perches on the top step and sips.
b2: {B.desc} hauls a crate up the next step along, then another.
{B.desc} backs through a door with a lamp and a rolled rug.
{B.desc} carries a box to the new door and sets it down.
b3: {A} waves. {B.desc} waves back with a free hand and nearly drops the crate.
{A} lifts a hand to {B.desc} across the landing.
{A} waves once at {B.desc} and goes back to the cup.

log: Overheard: {A} calls: "Welcome to the row, neighbor! Shout if you need a hand."
Overheard: {B.desc} calls back: "Thank you! I will!"

storylets.title: Reading the notice board
storylets.note: Townspeople read posted notices about changes in the city. Spreads opinion without conclusions.

A.desc: an adult at a notice board

b1: {A} reads a sheet pinned to the board with a finger tracing the lines.
{A} stops at the notice board and reads from top to bottom.
{A} scans a printed bulletin and taps the corner.
b2: {B.desc} comes up beside {A} and says something about the new rules.
{A} and {B.desc} talk in low tones, heads near the board.
{B.desc} points at a line and {A} answers.
b3: {A} shrugs and turns away, shaking {A.his} head.
{A} shakes {A.his} head, shrugs, and wanders off.
{A} turns away from {B.desc} and heads for the stalls.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "They'll build over it all and call it progress."
Overheard: {A} says: "It's about time somebody fixed the lift. I say let them."

storylets.title: Everyone looks up
storylets.note: A crowd watches construction. Cheap texture; reacts to the player's hand.

b1: {A} stands at a fence and watches a crane lift a beam.
{A} stays at the barrier with a cup, head back.
{A} stops at the edge of a plot and watches the work.
{A} lingers by the fence while a drone ferries steel.
b2: {A} points at the crane arm and says something aloud.
{A} gestures toward the swinging beam.
{A} indicates the half-built frame to a passing stranger.
{A} points at a pair of workers on a gantry.
b3: {A} wanders off after a few minutes, still looking back.
{A} walks away and glances up one more time.
{A} heads on down the block.
{A} turns away from the fence and goes.
